description: General vendor invoice and municipal bill extraction for vendor and city-issued billing documents.

vendor_name_extract.description: Name of the company, supplier, contractor, tradesperson, service provider, utility, or vendor issuing the invoice and requesting payment, exactly as clearly printed on the document. Read it from clearly printed text — for example the remittance or payment return slip, the 'remit to' or 'make cheque payable to' line, the footer legal name or a 'does business as' clause, the vendor contact block, or a website domain — rather than a stylized logo or graphic wordmark. When the name appears both as a stylized logo and as printed body text, use the printed text. Return the printed vendor name verbatim; do not paraphrase, shorten, or invent. Do not return the customer, Invoice To party, Bill To party, property manager, property owner, tenant, attention line, technician, or contact person.

vendor_name_generate.description: Common name of the company, supplier, contractor, tradesperson, service provider, utility, or vendor issuing the invoice and requesting payment. Read the vendor name from clearly printed text — for example the remittance or payment return slip, the 'remit to' or 'make cheque payable to' line, the footer legal name or a 'does business as' clause, the vendor contact block, or a website domain — rather than a stylized logo or graphic wordmark. When the name appears both as a stylized logo and as printed body text, use the printed text. Return the short common name the vendor is known by (for example 'FortisBC', 'BC Hydro'), not the full legal-entity suffix such as 'Energy Inc.', 'Inc.', or 'Ltd'. Do not return the customer, Invoice To party, Bill To party, property manager, property owner, tenant, attention line, technician, or contact person.

invoice_date.description: Date the invoice was issued. May be labeled Invoice Date, Date, Billing Date, Issue Date, Tax Invoice Date, Statement Date, or Notice Date. Return the issue date, not the due date, service date, or delivery date.

payment_due_date.description: Date payment is due. May be labeled Due Date, Payment Due Date, Payable By, Due On, or Balance Due Date. Return only an explicitly printed calendar date. Do not infer from invoice date, terms, or amount. If none is printed, return null.

invoice_number.description: Unique invoice identifier assigned by the vendor for this invoice. Prefer the value in the invoice header or top-right invoice table that is directly labeled Invoice #, Invoice No., Invoice Number, Inv #, Inv No., Tax Invoice No., Bill Number, or Document Number. The invoice number is often near the invoice date. If the document includes both an invoice page and a work order page, prefer the value labeled Invoice # on the invoice page; use a standalone '#:' value on the work order page only if it matches the invoice page number. Return only the identifier value, not the label. Do not return P.O. No., PO #, PO number, job number, work order number, project number, reference number, customer number, account number, vendor GST number, tax ID, phone number, postal code, license number, product registration number, date, subtotal, GST amount, total amount, balance due, or service address.

po_or_job_number_extract.description: Purchase order, job, work order, contract, project, or reference number. It is exactly 8 digits and always starts with 110 or 330 (for example 11024580 or 33001022). The digits may be printed with spaces between them (for example '1102 4580'); remove the spaces and return the 8 digits only, with no letters, dashes, or other punctuation. May be labeled PO #, P.O. No., Purchase Order, Customer PO, Job #, Job No., Job Number, Work Order, WO, Contract #, Contract No., Contract Number, Project No., Site Ref, Customer Ref, or Reference — or may appear unlabeled or after a bare '#'. Ignore candidates containing letters, and ignore values with 9 or more digits even when they carry a PO label — look elsewhere on the document for the 8-digit number starting with 110 or 330. If both a PO and a Job number exist, return the PO number. Return null if no 8-digit value starting with 110 or 330 is present.

po_or_job_number_generate.description:
Determine the buyer's purchase order or job number for this invoice. Reason step by step over the entire document:
1. The number is exactly 8 digits and always starts with 110 or 330 (examples: 11024580, 33001022). This format rule is absolute: a value that does not match it is never the answer, no matter how it is labeled.
2. Scan the whole document — header, bill-to / sold-to / customer block, subject and reference lines, contract lines, line-item descriptions, and footer — and collect every digit sequence that could match. Digits may be printed with spaces between them (for example '1102 4580' means 11024580); remove spaces before testing the format.
3. Candidates may be labeled PO #, P.O. No., Purchase Order, Customer PO, Job #, Job No., Job Number, Work Order, WO, Contract #, Contract No., Contract Number, Project No., Site Ref, Customer Ref, or Reference — but the number often appears unlabeled, after a bare '#', or immediately next to the customer name (for example 'NOBLE & ASSOCIATES PROPERTY MANAGEMENT # 11022266' means the number is 11022266).
4. If a labeled value fails the rule in step 1 (for example a 9-digit value on a 'Customer PO No.' line), discard it and keep looking — the correct 8-digit 110/330 number is usually printed elsewhere on the document, such as a Contract # or Job # line.
5. Never answer with a GST registration number, phone number, fax number, invoice number, account number, customer number, quote number, or any part of an address or date.
6. If multiple distinct matching numbers exist, prefer the one labeled PO; if the same number repeats, return it once.
Return only the 8 digits, with no spaces or punctuation. Before answering, verify your answer is exactly 8 digits and starts with 110 or 330. Return an empty string only if, after scanning the entire document, no 8-digit number starting with 110 or 330 appears anywhere.

gst_amount_extract.description: Canadian GST (5%) amount charged. Prefer the amount directly labeled GST, G.S.T., GST@5.0%, GST 5%, or Goods and Services Tax. Return the numeric amount, not the rate. If a separate provincial sales tax (PST) line is present, return only the GST line, not PST and not Total Tax. Use Total Tax only when there is no separate GST line and no other tax types are present. Do not return the GST registration number, subtotal, total, or balance due.

gst_amount_generate.description: Determine the Canadian GST (5%) amount charged on this invoice. Prefer the amount labeled GST, G.S.T., GST@5.0%, GST 5%, or Goods and Services Tax. Return the numeric amount, not the rate. If a separate provincial sales tax (PST) line is present, return only the GST line, not PST and not Total Tax. Use Total Tax only when there is no separate GST line and no other tax types are present. Do not return the GST registration number, subtotal, total, or balance due. Return an empty value if no GST is charged.

total_invoice_amount_extract.description: Final amount the recipient must pay, including all taxes and charges. Prefer values labeled Total, Invoice Total, Amount Due, Balance Due, Total Due, Grand Total, Amount Payable, or Please Pay. If Total and Balance Due are both present and equal, return that amount. Do not return subtotal, GST, amount paid, or a line amount.

total_invoice_amount_generate.description: Determine the final amount the recipient must pay, including all taxes and charges. Prefer values labeled Total, Invoice Total, Amount Due, Balance Due, Total Due, Grand Total, Amount Payable, or Please Pay. If Total and Balance Due are both present and equal, return that amount. Do not return the subtotal, the GST amount, an amount already paid, or an individual line amount.

service_address_extract.description: Address where the work, service, delivery, security monitoring, fire monitoring, repair, utility service, or billed property is located. Treat labels in this priority order: 1) SHIP TO / Ship To / Shipped To / Ship-to, especially when followed by text such as "the Premises", "Premises", "Site", or "Site Location"; 2) Service Address, Service Location, Site Address, Site Location, Job Address, Work Location, Property Address, Premises, Installation Address, or Service For; 3) for municipal bills only, the assessed or billed property address. When a document has both SOLD TO / Customer / Bill To / Invoice To and SHIP TO / Premises / Site blocks, always return the SHIP TO / Premises / Site address, not the SOLD TO or customer mailing address. For The Radius Group invoices, the service address is the address directly under SHIP TO (the "Premises"). In that layout, exclude the customer/company name line and return only the street, city, province/state, and postal code if printed. Example: if the block is "SHIP TO (the Premises) / 1100289 BC LTD / 1606 Broadway W / Vancouver, BC", return "1606 Broadway W\nVancouver, BC". Do not return the vendor's own office address, remittance address, logo/header address, SOLD TO address, Invoice To address, Bill To address, customer mailing address, account owner, property manager name, or company name line.

service_address_generate.description: Determine the address where the work, service, delivery, security monitoring, fire monitoring, repair, utility service, or billed property is located, and return it as a clean address. Prioritise the SHIP TO / Ship To / Shipped To block (especially when labelled 'the Premises', 'Premises', 'Site', or 'Site Location'), then Service Address, Service Location, Site Address, Site Location, Job Address, Work Location, Property Address, Installation Address, or Service For; for municipal bills, the assessed or billed property address. When both a SOLD TO / Customer / Bill To / Invoice To block and a SHIP TO / Premises / Site block are present, always use the SHIP TO / Premises / Site location, never the SOLD TO or customer mailing address. Assemble the street, city, province/state, and postal code. Exclude the customer/company name line, the vendor's own office or remittance address, any logo or header address, the property manager name, and the account owner. Return an empty string if undeterminable.

bill_type.description: Classify by WHO issued the document/invoice/bill and what kind of biller they are — never by who is being billed. Municipal bill is issued by a government or municipal body — a city, town, regional district, or municipal utility — OR is an energy or water utility account statement (natural gas, electricity, water, sewer, stormwater), whether that utility is a government body or a private utility company. Includes energy and water/sewer/stormwater utility charges, business license and permit renewal fees, property tax, and other government or city-issued charges — including a garbage, waste, or recycling charge that appears on a government or city-issued utility bill. Return "municipal" for FortisBC natural gas bills, BC Hydro electricity bills, city water/sewer/stormwater bills, and similar energy or water utility account statements. Commercial document or invoice is issued by a private business — tradespeople and contractors (plumbing, electrical, HVAC, roofing, carpentry, restoration, general contracting, appliance repair, pest control), grounds and landscaping services, fire inspection service, private garbage, waste, and recycling collection or hauling companies (for example Waste Connections, GFL, Waste Management), private telecom, internet, and phone companies, insurers, and general suppliers. A private garbage/recycling/waste-hauling company that issues its own service invoice is commercial even though it handles waste; only a garbage or waste charge issued by a government or city body is municipal. If you cannot confirm the bill is a government or municipal charge or an energy or water utility account statement, output 'commercial'.

is_handwritten.description: Classify yes when any important field (vendor name, total amount, service address, GST amount, or PO/job number) appears handwritten or manually filled in. Classify no when those fields are printed or digitally generated, even if there are handwritten notes, signatures, or checkboxes elsewhere. This value is informational only.

invoice_description.description: One short sentence (15 words or fewer) describing what this invoic is for, from the line items, Service For, or notes. Do not include vendor name, numbers, address, date, tax, or total. Do not mention GST. Examples: 'Lawn maintenance service in March.' 'Electrical repair work.' 'Monthly water utility charges in June.' 'Annual business license renewal for 2026.' Return an empty string if undeterminable.

anomaly_flag.description: Note genuine anomalies for a reviewer: vendor name missing, total amount missing, a total amount lower than the GST amount when GST is present, a GST amount that is clearly not about 5% of the pre-tax amount when GST is present, a suspiciously round total with no itemisation, or duplicate-looking line items. Do not flag a missing invoice number or a missing payment due date. Return an empty string if nothing is unusual.
